info.title: NimbusPost — Partner API v2
info.summary: The modern NimbusPost partner surface — create & ship orders, track shipments, manage returns/QC, warehouses, manifests, NDR, your wallet, and outbound webhooks, behind a single API-key pair.
info.description:
## Overview

The **Partner API v2** is NimbusPost's modern JSON-over-HTTPS REST surface and the **recommended** API for all new integrations. A single API-key pair authenticates every call. It covers the full shipping lifecycle:

| Area | What you can do |
| --- | --- |
| **Orders** | Create forward & reverse (return) orders, list, get, cancel |
| **Returns & QC** | Attach / read quality-check findings (image URLs + condition flags) on a return |
| **Shipments** | One-shot create+book, book an existing order, cancel by AWB, request pickup, generate labels |
| **Tracking** | Single-AWB summary, bulk lookup (≤100 AWBs) |
| **Serviceability & Couriers** | Rate + serviceability check, courier catalogue |
| **Manifests** | Create a manifest from a set of AWBs (≤200) |
| **NDR** | List exception shipments, submit an NDR action |
| **Warehouses** | List, OTP-verify a contact phone, find-or-create (pickup + RTO) |
| **Wallet** | Read your current balance |
| **Webhooks** | Register/manage outbound webhook subscriptions for real-time events |

Every endpoint is reached through the NimbusPost API gateway; downstream services are not directly accessible. Legacy surfaces (the `ship.nimbuspost.com/api/*` public API and the per-partner `/v1`, `/unicommerce`, `/easyecom`, `/omsguru` adapters) remain available for existing integrations, but new integrators should build against v2.

## Base URL & paths

```
https://api-v2.nimbuspost.com
```

The Partner API v2 lives on its own host. All v2 endpoints live under the `/v2` path — e.g. `/v2/orders`, `/v2/shipments`, `/v2/tracking/AWB123456789`. Unlike NimbusPost's internal services (which sit under `/api/v1/...`), the v2 partner paths are intentionally clean — `/v2/orders`, **never** `/v2/api/v1/orders`.

## Authentication — the `npk_` API-key pair

Every v2 request authenticates with an **API-key pair** sent as **two headers, both required**:

| Header | Value | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x-api-key` | The public key id (always `npk_`-prefixed) | `npk_a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8` |
| `x-api-secret` | The matching secret half | `s3cr3t-…-24-bytes` |

If **either** header is missing the request is rejected with `401 Unauthorized`. This is a header **pair**, not a `Bearer` token.

```bash
curl -X GET https://api-v2.nimbuspost.com/v2/wallet/balance \
  -H "x-api-key: npk_a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8" \
  -H "x-api-secret: s3cr3t-...-24-bytes" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

### Generating a key

Create keys in the **NimbusPost dashboard → Settings → API Keys**. When you create or rotate a key, the response shows the **key id and the secret exactly once** — store the secret immediately; it is never retrievable again. Rotate to mint a new secret; revoke to disable a key. On create you set:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string (1–100) | yes | Human label, e.g. `OMS integration` |
| `role` | enum `admin` \| `viewer` | no (default `viewer`) | `admin` = full access; `viewer` = read-only |
| `piiAccess` | boolean | no (default `false`) | When `true`, responses return **unmasked** PII (customer phone, email, address). Independent of role. |
| `ipAllowlist` | string[] (≤50) | no | **Exact** IPv4/IPv6 addresses only — **CIDR ranges are not supported**. Empty/omitted = any source IP. |
| `expiresAt` | ISO 8601 datetime | no | Omit for a non-expiring key. |
| `type` | enum | no (default `generic`) | Target contract; new integrations use `generic`. |

### Roles, PII, IP allowlist, expiry

- **Roles.** A key carries exactly one of two roles — `admin` (full access) or `viewer` (read-only). The role expands server-side to the same `module:action` scope set NimbusPost uses internally, so a `viewer` key **cannot** create/cancel/book (it gets `401` on mutating routes — order create, shipment create/book/cancel, warehouse create, NDR action, webhook create/update/delete).
- **PII access** is a separate flag (`piiAccess`). Without it, customer PII is **masked** in every response. Grant it only to keys that genuinely need unmasked contact details.
- **IP allowlist.** If set, requests are accepted only from the listed **exact** source IPs (matched against the gateway-resolved client IP). CIDR ranges are rejected at key-creation time. Off-allowlist requests fail authentication (`401`).
- **Expiry.** After `expiresAt` the key stops authenticating. Omit `expiresAt` for a non-expiring key.

### Channel binding (important)

Each API key is **bound to an `api`-type channel**. Orders you create with that key are **attributed to that channel** in your NimbusPost account. If you run multiple integrations, mint one key per integration so reporting stays clean.

## Conventions

- **Content type.** Send and accept `application/json`. Set `Content-Type: application/json` on every request with a body and `Accept: application/json` on every request.
- **Success envelope.** Every successful response is wrapped as `{ "success": true, "data": { … }, "meta": { "requestId": "…" } }`. Paginated lists carry `meta.pagination` (`{ page, perPage, total, totalPages }`).
- **Error envelope.** Every failure is wrapped as `{ "success": false, "error": { type, title, status, code, detail }, "meta": { requestId, traceId } }`. **Branch on `error.code`** (stable machine code — `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, …), not on the human-readable `error.detail`. Quote `meta.requestId` when contacting support; `meta.traceId` is the engineering correlation id.
- **Field casing on the wire.** Order / shipment / warehouse request & response bodies use **`snake_case`** field names (e.g. `order_number`, `payment_mode`, `order_collectable_amount`). The tracking, courier, serviceability and webhook surfaces use **`camelCase`** (e.g. `orderId`, `courierName`, `lastDeliveryAt`). Each endpoint documents its exact shape.
- **Phones are numbers.** Order `shipping_address.phone` and warehouse contact `phone` are sent as **numeric** values (10-digit), not strings.

## Passthrough bodies

Several v2 endpoints (`POST /v2/orders`, `POST /v2/shipments`, `/v2/shipments/book`, `/v2/shipments/pickup`, `/v2/shipments/labels`, `/v2/serviceability`, `/v2/orders/{orderId}/cancel`, `/v2/ndr/{awb}/action`) accept a body that v2 **passes through verbatim** to the owning service's canonical contract (order-service / allocation-service), which performs the authoritative validation. The request schemas documented here reflect that downstream contract; additional fields are tolerated and forwarded.

## Common HTTP statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `201` | Created (order create, shipment create+book, manifest create, webhook create) |
| `204` | No content (webhook delete) |
| `401` | Missing/invalid API-key pair, off-allowlist source IP, or a `viewer` key on a mutating route |
| `404` | Resource not found (order, AWB, webhook) |
| `422` / `400` | Validation failed (bad/missing fields) |
| `429` | Rate limited (see `Retry-After`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset`) |

post.summary: Create an order (forward or reverse) — no booking
post.description:
Creates an order **without** booking a courier. To create AND book in one call, use `POST /v2/shipments`.

**Reverse / returns** ride the SAME endpoint: set `order_type: "reverse"`, point `parent_order_id` at the original forward order, and supply a `return_reason` plus an optional `return_reason_note`. **Reverse with QC at pickup**: add `qc_status: true` and a `qc_data[]` array (image URLs + condition flags); you can also set/replace QC after creation via `PATCH /v2/orders/{orderId}/qc`.

The body follows the order-service create contract (passed through verbatim and authoritatively validated there). Requires an `admin` key.

post.summary: Create a shipment (create order + book in one call)
post.description: The one-shot "create waybill" flow: creates the order, auto-allocates the **top-ranked serviceable courier** (or honours a pinned `courier_id`), books, and returns the order **and** the booking (AWB, `courier_name`, `price` — where `price.total` is the amount deducted from your wallet — `label_url`, and the `tracking_url` / `tracking_short_url`). If no courier is serviceable the order is created but **not** booked, and the `400` error says so — re-attempt booking once a courier is available. Requires an `admin` key.

post.summary: Find or create a warehouse (OTP-verified pickup contact required)
post.description:
Upsert by **name** (case-insensitive — the name is the identifier); the response carries a `created` flag. **The pickup contact phone MUST be OTP-verified first** — set `contact_person.phone_verified: true` + `contact_person.verification_id` from a prior `POST /v2/warehouses/otp/verify` (`purpose: "pickup"`), else the request is rejected with `422`.

**RTO (return-to-origin):** either reuse an existing warehouse via `rto_warehouse_id`, OR supply a full `rto_address` + `rto_contact_person` + `rto_name`. When you supply an `rto_contact_person`, ITS `phone_verified` must be `true` with a matching `rto` `verification_id`. See the *Warehouse mandatory-OTP flow* below. Requires an `admin` key.

apiKeyId.name: x-api-key
apiKeyId.description: The public **key id** half of the API-key pair, always `npk_`-prefixed (e.g. `npk_a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8`). MUST be sent together with `x-api-secret` — both schemes are required on every request. Mint keys in the dashboard (Settings → API Keys).

apiKeySecret.name: x-api-secret
apiKeySecret.description: The **secret** half of the API-key pair, shown exactly once on key create/rotate. MUST be sent together with `x-api-key`. Off-allowlist source IPs, expired keys, and (on mutating routes) `viewer`-role keys are rejected with `401`.

SuccessMeta.description: Response metadata present on every success.

requestId.description: Customer-facing correlation id. Quote it when contacting NimbusPost support.

PaginatedMeta.description: Response metadata for paginated list endpoints.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Standard error envelope. Branch on `error.code` (stable), not `error.detail` (human-readable, may change).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code — branch on this.

detail.description: Human-readable description, safe to surface to end users.

requestId.description: Customer-facing correlation id. Quote it for support.

traceId.description: Engineering correlation id (OTel trace id), present on errors.

ShippingAddress.description: Customer delivery address. Sent in `snake_case`; `phone` and `pincode` are numbers.

Package.description: Parcel dimensions & weight. Weight in grams; L/W/H in centimetres.

QcImage.description: One inspected image on a QC line. Partners supply a public URL — there is NO multipart upload on v2.

QcLine.description: A single QC finding — condition flags + identifiers + inspected image URLs.

CreateOrderRequest.description: Order create payload (order-service contract, passed through verbatim). Use `order_type: "forward"`/`"b2c"` for a normal order; `order_type: "reverse"` for a return (then `parent_order_id` + `return_reason` are required, and you may attach QC via `qc_status` + `qc_data`). Additional order-service fields are tolerated and forwarded.

order_type.description: `forward` / `b2c` for a normal order; `reverse` for a return.

order_collectable_amount.description: Amount to collect on delivery. Required for COD.

parent_order_id.description: **Reverse only (required).** The original forward order id.

qc_status.description: **Reverse only.** `true` to attach QC at pickup (requires `qc_data`).

qc_data.description: **Reverse only, when `qc_status: true`.** QC findings per item.

channel_id.description: Override the channel attribution. By default the order is attributed to the API key's bound channel; a caller-supplied `channel_id` always wins.

TrackingSummary.description: Latest tracking + order summary. Exposes the **latest** event only (`latest`); subscribe to the `tracking.updated` webhook for the full history.

shippingAddress.description: City/state/pincode only (masked unless the key has `piiAccess`).

Booking.description: Booking result — AWB, courier, price breakdown, label, and tracking URLs. `price.total` is the amount (in rupees) actually deducted from your wallet for this booking.

total.description: The total charge (in rupees) deducted from your wallet for this booking.

tracking_url.description: Customer-facing tracking page URL (the long URL). Always present.

tracking_short_url.description: Public short-domain redirect to the tracking page. May be an empty string when the short-link service was unreachable at booking time (the link is minted best-effort) — fall back to `tracking_url`.

pincode.description: Pincode (string). The Postman example also sends it as a number; both are accepted.

WarehouseContact.description: A warehouse contact. Its `phone` MUST be OTP-verified first — set `phone_verified: true` + the `verification_id` from `/otp/verify` (matching `purpose`).

CreateWarehouseRequest.description: Find-or-create a warehouse by **name** (case-insensitive — the name is the identifier). The pickup `contact_person.phone` MUST be OTP-verified first; when an `rto_contact_person` is supplied, ITS phone too (`purpose: "rto"`). Either reuse an existing warehouse as RTO via `rto_warehouse_id`, OR supply a full `rto_address` + `rto_contact_person` + `rto_name`.

rto_warehouse_id.description: Reuse an existing warehouse as the RTO location (no RTO OTP needed).

WebhookSubscription.description: A webhook subscription (no secret — the secret is shown only on create / secret-rotation).

lastDeliveryStatus.description: Last HTTP status from the endpoint, or null.

autoPausedAt.description: Set when repeated delivery failures auto-disabled the webhook.

secret.description: HMAC signing secret — shown ONCE; verify the x-nimbus-signature header with it.

CreatedWebhookSubscription.description: Newly created subscription — includes the one-time signing secret.

WebhookDelivery.description: One delivery attempt-set per (subscription, event). Dedupe on the `x-nimbus-delivery` header — buckets are at-least-once streams.

attempts.description: POST attempts so far (bus retries included).

responseStatus.description: Last HTTP status from the endpoint, or null on a network error.

status.description: HTTP status returned by the endpoint, or null on error.

warehouse_address.description: Pickup warehouse address; null when unassigned.

Order.description: Canonical order. Buyer PII fields (name/email/phone/address/gst) are masked unless the key has PII access.

CancelledShipment.description: A previously-cancelled shipment on the order.

OrderDetail.description: Order detail — the full order plus its cancelled-shipment history.

created.description: True if newly created, false if an existing one matched the name.

FindOrCreateWarehouse.description: Find-or-create warehouse result (the warehouse plus a `created` flag).

verification_id.description: Pass this (with phone_verified) when creating the warehouse.

RateResult.description: Per-courier rate breakdown (paise). Slab/itemized detail omitted for brevity.

excluded.description: Couriers excluded from this quote, with reasons.
